newsitem.title: USA: Digital profit down sharply but better than expected.
newsitem.headline: Digital profit down sharply but better than expected.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp. said Thursday it earned $51 million in its third quarter, down sharply from $124 million a year earlier but slightly better than Wall Street had expected.
Digital, which makes computers, computer chips and computer systems, said its sales fell to $3.3 billion from $3.6 billion.
The sharp drop in income had been expected on Wall Street, but Digital's stock surged $2.25 to $28.375 a share in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Digital said the profits were equal to 27 cents a share, down from 74 cents a share a year earlier. Analysts had forecast that Digital would earn 24 cents a share, according to estimates compiled by First Call.
"Although revenue was not where we wanted it to be, it was within our expectations with progress in key strategic areas," said Chairman Robert B. Palmer.
Revenue from sales of products fell to $1.84 billion from $2.06 billion and revenue from services fell to $1.48 billion from $1.57 billion.
Palmer said Digital is making progress in a number of strategic areas.

"Our Internet business, which includes servers, networking products, software and services, achieved good growth during the quarter with total revenue now more than $1 billion on an annual basis," he said.
Analysts were concerned about Digital's lack of comment on its product line designed around its Alpha microprocessors.
Digital's Alpha products are built around its Alpha microprocessor chip that it developed as a high-speed alternative to Intel Corp. microprocessors.
"The fact that they didn't comment on Alpha means that Alpha probably wasn't very good," said John Jones, an analyst with Salomon Brothers.
In comments made subsequent to the release of its results, Digital said sales of its Alpha products increased by 6 percent in the third quarter.
Gross margin fell to 33.4 percent from 34.6 percent a year ago but was up from 32.9 percent in the fiscal second quarter.

The company also said it is making progress in sales to Internet service providers, as over 200 in 37 countries are using Digital's servers running Alpha and Intel processors, its storage systems and networking products.
Digital said its services business met its near-term objectives for revenue and gross margin. Services gross margins were 31 percent, versus 31.3 percent a year ago.
